rules.requirement: Reuse the exact existing WordPress display label only when its meaning and specificity match the inspected evidence. Prior usage is not semantic validation.

Retrieve concept definition, preferred label, code, synonyms, version and active/obsolete status. Record exact, synonym, broader, narrower, ambiguous, or unmapped relation. Broader/narrower/ambiguous mappings require curator review. Do not invent a code.
Any label not confirmed as registered in the same WordPress field requires needs curator decision. Supply alternatives, evidence and the reason no existing term fits.

Unseen in usage is a review trigger, not proof of a new registered term. A complete authorized term export is needed to prove registry absence; stale registry evidence leaves current membership unverified.

Consult the NCI Imaging Submission Model first and the GDC owning schema with its referenced definitions next. Record repository commit/path/field. External enums do not automatically become WordPress terms and GDC field values need not match TCIA values.

Use known primary disease site; preserve metastatic site, scanned anatomy and annotation targets separately. Unknown primary, systemic disease, mixed cohorts and non-disease study contexts require evidence and review when no faithful label/mapping exists.

Review every download independently using actual content or an authoritative inventory. Store transfer container and manifest format separately from payload format. ZIP may remain appropriate for a ZIP payload; do not remove existing labels automatically.

Use unable to verify for unavailable ontology/registry/content evidence. Use needs curator decision for a proposed new value or ambiguous mapping; record verification gaps separately. Neither state is approval.

Retain the standalone Non-Cancer label as the TCIA catch-all filter for documented non-cancer cohorts or components, including mixed cohorts. Also assign supported specific disease or cohort-context labels (for example Vestibular Schwannoma (non-cancer), COVID-19 Infection (non-cancer), or Healthy Subject). Verify faithful NCIt mappings for specific concepts and registry membership for all display labels. A parenthetical non-cancer string is not standalone filter membership. Do not infer Healthy Subject from nonmalignancy or force one NCIt disease mapping onto this TCIA discovery grouping. Review synthetic phantom cases under the species/Not Applicable decision. Dataset-level labels are not patient-level assertions.

Represent phantom identity in species. Retain supported simulated disease and anatomical context labels when applicable; do not automatically replace them with Not Applicable. Confirmed example: VICTRE retains Breast Cancer and Non-Cancer with Computational Phantom species. Use Not Applicable where disease/site context does not apply. Do not describe computational subjects as Healthy Subject.
